summary: Early December in Berlin is cold and grey, usually about 0–5°, with short days: dark by about 16:00. The Christmas markets are open. Sunday is your travel day, and most shops are closed on Sundays.

pack.why: About 0–5°, and colder in the wind
Cold outside, warm inside trains and museums
Needed at the airport and the hotel
On the back of your Dutch health insurance card
Market stalls and small bars often want cash

pack.text: Snacks, water and something to read
pack.why: The train to Berlin takes about 6 hours

know.title: Money
know.text: Euro. Cards are accepted in more places than before, but many small cafés, bars and market stalls still want cash.

know.title: Plugs
know.text: Type F, 230 V: the same as in the Netherlands. No adapter needed.

know.title: Tipping
know.text: Round up or add about 5–10%. Say the total you want to pay when you hand over the money or card, for example "25, bitte".

know.title: Christmas markets
know.text: Mulled wine (Glühwein) comes with a cup deposit (Pfand) of a few euros. Give the cup back to get it, or keep it.

know.title: Sunday
know.text: Most shops and supermarkets are closed on Sunday; shops in the main stations stay open. Some Advent Sundays are shopping Sundays in Berlin, so check before you plan to shop.

know.title: Emergency
know.text: Call 112 for an ambulance or fire, 110 for the police.

know.title: A few words
know.text: Hallo (hello) · Danke (thank you) · Die Rechnung, bitte (the bill, please).

know.title: Water
know.text: Tap water is safe. In restaurants, water is usually bottled and you pay for it.

items.title: Train from Amsterdam (Friday)
items.text: The train arrives at Berlin Hauptbahnhof. On German trains a seat reservation is optional; check if your ticket has one, otherwise look for free seats without a reservation sign. The train has a restaurant car.

items.title: Tickets in the city
items.text: An AB ticket covers the city. Buy it in the BVG app or at a machine. Validate a paper ticket in the small stamping machine before you get on.

items.title: To BER airport (Sunday)
items.text: The FEX airport express leaves Hauptbahnhof every 15 minutes and takes about 23 minutes. You need an ABC ticket (€5.00). For the 17:00 Lufthansa flight, leave the centre by about 15:00.

items.title: Connection in Frankfurt
items.text: You change planes in Frankfurt with only 35 minutes. Both flights are Lufthansa, so your bag should go through to Amsterdam. Go straight to the next gate; Frankfurt is large.

sources.title: VBB: by public transport to BER
